key_insight: Spectral bias can be explained by the graded eigen-structure of a dynamics matrix, showing why shallow networks learn sinusoidal components first and generalizing beyond Fourier-domain aliasing.
engineering_relevance: This framework can guide architecture and activation choices when designing models that should capture low-frequency structure before high-frequency detail.
method: Expand network outputs as a general Fourier series in an orthogonal polynomial basis.
Derive gradient-descent dynamics for the series coefficients as an ODE system with dynamics matrix H.
Analyze H’s eigenvalue decay and eigenvector shapes to explain learning order and activation dependence.
evidence_signal: The paper is theoretical and uses analysis of the dynamics matrix H rather than new experimental data or benchmark evaluation in the abstract.
watch_item: The framework is asymptotic and depends on orthogonal polynomial assumptions, so practical finite-sample behavior and implementation details may differ.
paper_title: Why Shallow Neural Networks Learn Sinusoidal Components First: An Orthogonal Polynomial Dynamics Framework
